title: Blocky proline/glutamine patterns in the SFPQ intrinsically disordered region dictate paraspeckle formation as a distinct membraneless organelle.
authors: Takakuwa, Hiro; Yoda, Takao; Yamazaki, Tomohiro; Hirose, Tetsuro
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SFPQ无序区中脯氨酸/谷氨酰胺块状模式对paraspeckle形成与区隔化的作用，涉及蛋白质相分离和分子动力学模拟，但核心对象为蛋白质-蛋白质/RNA介导的无膜细胞器，非TF-DNA互作体系，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Membraneless organelles (MLOs) formed through phase separation play crucial roles in various cellular processes. Many MLOs remain spatially compartmentalized, avoiding fusion or engulfment. MLOs are formed by dynamic multivalent interactions, often mediated by proteins with intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). However, the molecular principles behind how IDRs maintain MLO independence remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the proline/glutamine (P/Q)-rich IDR of SFPQ, a protein identified as a key factor in segregating paraspeckles from nuclear speckles. Paraspeckle segregation analyses, using SFPQ mutants tethered to NEAT1_2 long noncoding RNA, revealed that P/Q residues within the SFPQ IDR, conserved from humans to zebrafish, are crucial for its segregation activity. Beyond amino acid composition, the blocky patterns of P/Q residues, in which proline- and glutamine-rich blocks are repetitively arranged, are required for segregation from nuclear speckles. Among human IDRs exhibiting PQ-block patterns, BRD4 IDR shows strong sequence similarity to the SFPQ IDR and exhibits comparable segregation activity. Molecular dynamics simulation suggests that the PQ-blocky patterns required for the paraspeckle segregation do not correlate with the IDR characteristics necessary for self-assembly. Thus, these data suggest that the PQ-blocky patterns in IDRs represent a previously uncharacterized property that contributes to MLO independence, possibly through a mechanism distinct from the conventional phase separation-promoting function of IDRs.
abstract_zh: 通过相分离（phase separation）形成的无膜细胞器（membraneless organelles, MLOs）在多种细胞过程中发挥关键作用。许多MLOs保持空间分隔状态，避免融合或被吞噬。MLOs由动态多价相互作用形成，通常由含有内在无序区域（intrinsically disordered regions, IDRs）的蛋白质介导。然而，IDRs如何维持MLOs独立性的分子原理仍知之甚少。在此，我们研究了SFPQ的脯氨酸/谷氨酰胺（proline/glutamine, P/Q）富集IDR，SFPQ被鉴定为将副斑（paraspeckles）与核斑（nuclear speckles）分离的关键因子。使用锚定至NEAT1_2长链非编码RNA的SFPQ突变体进行的副斑分离分析揭示，SFPQ IDR中从人类到斑马鱼保守的P/Q残基对其分离活性至关重要。除氨基酸组成外，P/Q残基的块状模式（其中脯氨酸和谷氨酰胺富集块重复排列）对于从核斑中分离是必需的。在表现出PQ块状模式的人类IDRs中，BRD4 IDR与SFPQ IDR显示出强序列相似性，并表现出相当的分离活性。分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟表明，副斑分离所需的PQ块状模式与自组装所需的IDR特征不相关。因此，这些数据表明，IDRs中的PQ块状模式代表了一种先前未表征的特性，有助于MLO独立性，可能通过不同于IDRs常规促进相分离功能的机制发挥作用。
